anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through series resistor R60 to ESTOP_OUT as well. Both LED terminals therefore sit on the same net, so no current can flow through LED2. The pattern differs from LED1 (D30.3/A1 on the enable net, D30.1/K1 through R59 to GND), which is wired correctly.
anomalies.expected: R60 should return the LED cathode to GND, with the anode driven from ESTOP_OUT, so that LED2 indicates the e-stop output state as LED1 does.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop status indicator LED never lights. The LED is dead, which removes a visual cue for the e-stop state, although the e-stop chain itself is unaffected.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 ideal-diode PMOS Q1 has its source (pin 2) on the +5V output net and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The controller's VIN (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and its SENSE (U6.6) is on +5V. In the LTC4412 arrangement the FET source should face the VIN supply and the drain the load.
anomalies.expected: PMOS source on the VIN (USB VBUS) side and drain on the +5V side, so that the body diode blocks reverse current from +5V back to USB and the controller enables forward conduction from VBUS.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The body diode of Q1 conducts from +5V back toward USB when the FET is off, so the reverse-current protection the design relies on fails and the USB power path may not deliver as intended.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three green/yellow status LEDs D4, D14 and D23 sit on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, and nothing else is connected to that net. It has no supply and no driver, so the LEDs have no drive path.
anomalies.expected: The LED anode supply net should be driven from a 3.3V rail, or from a switch or driver if the _SW name implies one.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity LEDs (via R2 and R3) and the PI activity LED (via R10) cannot light, so these status indicators are non-functional.
